  85 if (!scope) return { error: 'Scope failed.' }
  86 const angles = scope.angles.slice(0, MAX_ANGLES)
  87 log('Angles: ' + angles.map(a => a.label).join(', '))
  88 
  89 // ─── dedup + fetch-slot state ───
  90 const normURL = u => { try { const p = new URL(u); return (p.hostname.replace(/^www\./, '') + p.pathname.replace(/\/$/, '')).toLowerCase() } catch { return u.toLowerCase() } }
  91 const seen = new Set()
  92 const relRank = { high: 0, medium: 1, low: 2 }
  93 let fetchSlots = MAX_FETCH
  94 
  95 const SEARCH_PROMPT = a =>
  96   '## Web searcher: ' + a.label + '\nQuestion: "' + Q + '"\nAngle: ' + (a.rationale || '') + '\nQuery: `' + a.query + '`\n\n' +
  97   'PREFER the Bright Data CLI: run `bdata search "<query>" --json` via Bash FIRST (broader reach, fewer blocks). ' +
  98   'ALSO run WebSearch and merge both result sets. If `bdata` is missing or errors, fall back to WebSearch alone. ' +
  99   'Return the top 3-5 results most relevant to the ORIGINAL question. Skip SEO spam. Structured output only.'
 100 
 101 const FETCH_PROMPT = (s, ang) =>
 102   '## Source extractor\nQuestion: "' + Q + '"\nURL: ' + s.url + '\nTitle: ' + s.title + '\nVia: ' + ang + '\n\n' +
 103   '1. Fetch the page: PREFER `bdata scrape "<url>" --format markdown` via Bash (Bright Data Web Unlocker — handles blocks/paywalls). If `bdata` is missing or errors, use WebFetch instead.\n' +
 104   '2. Write the full extracted notes to a file under `' + SCRATCH + '/` — that path is RELATIVE TO THE CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY (the repo root); do not write under $HOME. mkdir -p it first. Return the path as scratchFile (CONTEXT FIREWALL — do not paste the full page back).\n' +
 105   '3. Return 2-4 FALSIFIABLE claims (each with a direct quote + central/supporting/tangential) and the source quality.\n' +
 106   'If both fetch methods fail or the page is irrelevant, return claims: [] and sourceQuality: "unreliable". Structured output only.'
 107 
 108 const VERIFY_PROMPT = (c, v) =>
 109   '## Adversarial verifier (voter ' + (v + 1) + '/' + VOTES_PER_CLAIM + ')\nBe skeptical — try to REFUTE.\n\n' +
 110   'Question: ' + Q + '\nClaim: "' + c.claim + '"\nSource: ' + c.sourceUrl + ' (' + c.sourceQuality + ')\nQuote: "' + c.quote + '"\n\n' +
 111   'WebSearch (or bdata) for contradicting evidence. refuted=true if unsupported by the quote / contradicted / ' +
 112   'low-quality source for a strong claim / outdated / marketing. Default to refuted=true if uncertain. Structured output only.'
 113 
 114 // ─── Search → dedup → fetch (pipelined, budget-gated) ───
 115 phase('Search')
 116 const fetched = await pipeline(
 117   angles,
 118   a => {
 119     if (!canAfford(6_000)) { log('budget gate: skipping search ' + a.label); return null }
 120     return agent(SEARCH_PROMPT(a), { label: 'search:' + a.label, phase: 'Search', schema: SEARCH_SCHEMA, model: 'haiku' })
 121       .then(r => r ? { angle: a.label, results: r.results } : null)
 122   },
 123   sr => {
 124     if (!sr) return null
 125     const novel = [...sr.results].sort((x, y) => relRank[x.relevance] - relRank[y.relevance]).filter(r => {
 126       const k = normURL(r.url)
 127       if (seen.has(k) || fetchSlots <= 0) return false
 128       seen.add(k); fetchSlots--; return true
 129     })
 130     return parallel(novel.map(s => () => {
 131       if (!canAfford(8_000)) { log('budget gate: skipping fetch ' + s.url); return null }
 132       let host = 'src'; try { host = new URL(s.url).hostname.replace(/^www\./, '') } catch {}
 133       return agent(FETCH_PROMPT(s, sr.angle), { label: 'fetch:' + host, phase: 'Fetch', schema: EXTRACT_SCHEMA, model: 'haiku' })
 134         .then(e => e ? { url: s.url, angle: sr.angle, sourceQuality: e.sourceQuality, scratchFile: e.scratchFile,
 135           claims: e.claims.map(c => ({ ...c, sourceUrl: s.url, sourceQuality: e.sourceQuality })) } : null)
 136         .catch(() => null)
 137     }))
 138   }
 139 )
 140 
 141 const sources = fetched.flat().filter(Boolean)
 142 const impRank = { central: 0, supporting: 1, tangential: 2 }
 143 const qualRank = { primary: 0, secondary: 1, blog: 2, forum: 3, unreliable: 4 }
 144 const claims = sources.flatMap(s => s.claims)
 145   .sort((a, b) => (impRank[a.importance] - impRank[b.importance]) || (qualRank[a.sourceQuality] - qualRank[b.sourceQuality]))
 146   .slice(0, MAX_VERIFY_CLAIMS)
 147 log('Fetched ' + sources.length + ' sources → verifying top ' + claims.length + ' claims · spent so far ' + Math.round(budget.spent() / 1000) + 'k')
 148 
 149 // ─── Verify (budget-gated per claim) ───
 150 phase('Verify')
 151 const voted = (await parallel(claims.map(c => () => {
 152   if (!canAfford(VOTES_PER_CLAIM * 5_000)) { log('budget gate: skipping verify of "' + c.claim.slice(0, 40) + '"'); return null }
 153   return parallel(Array.from({ length: VOTES_PER_CLAIM }, (_, v) => () =>
 154     agent(VERIFY_PROMPT(c, v), { label: 'v' + v, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA, model: 'sonnet' })
 155   )).then(vs => {
 156     const valid = vs.filter(Boolean)
 157     const refuted = valid.filter(x => x.refuted).length
 158     const survives = valid.length >= REFUTATIONS_REQUIRED && refuted < REFUTATIONS_REQUIRED
 159     log('"' + c.claim.slice(0, 45) + '": ' + (valid.length - refuted) + '-' + refuted + (survives ? ' ✓' : ' ✗'))
 160     return { ...c, refutedVotes: refuted, survives }
 161   })
 162 }))).filter(Boolean)
 163 
 164 const confirmed = voted.filter(c => c.survives)
 165 const killed = voted.filter(c => !c.survives)
 166 log('Verified ' + voted.length + ' → ' + confirmed.length + ' confirmed, ' + killed.length + ' killed')
 167 
 168 // ─── Synthesize — PINNED to Sonnet (never inherits Fable; that's the cost guarantee) ───
 169 phase('Synthesize')
 170 const block = confirmed.map((c, i) => '### [' + i + '] ' + c.claim + '\nVote ' + (VOTES_PER_CLAIM - c.refutedVotes) + '-' + c.refutedVotes +
 171   ' · ' + c.sourceUrl + ' (' + c.sourceQuality + ')\nQuote: "' + c.quote + '"').join('\n\n')
 172 
 173 const report = confirmed.length === 0 ? null : await agent(
 174   '## Synthesis\nQuestion: ' + Q + '\n\n' + confirmed.length + ' claims survived ' + VOTES_PER_CLAIM +
 175   '-vote verification. Merge duplicates, group into findings that answer the question, assign confidence, ' +
 176   'write a 3-5 sentence summary, list caveats + open questions.\n\n## Confirmed\n' + block + '\n\nStructured output only.',
 177   { label: 'synthesize', schema: REPORT_SCHEMA, model: 'sonnet' }
 178 )
 179 
 180 return {
 181   question: Q,
 182   ...(report || { summary: confirmed.length ? 'Synthesis skipped.' : 'No claims survived verification.', findings: [], caveats: '' }),
 183   scratchDir: SCRATCH,
 184   refuted: killed.map(c => ({ claim: c.claim, source: c.sourceUrl })),
 185   sources: sources.map(s => ({ url: s.url, quality: s.sourceQuality, file: s.scratchFile })),
 186   stats: {
 187     angles: angles.length, sources: sources.length, claimsVerified: voted.length,
 188     confirmed: confirmed.length, killed: killed.length,
 189     outputTokensSpent: budget.spent(),
 190     estimatedTotalTokens: budget.spent() * ioRatio,   // the figure that maps to your usage meter
 191     capTotalTokens: capTotal, outputCeiling: Math.round(outCeiling),
 192     hitBudgetGate: headroom() <= reserve,
 193   },
 194 }
references/routing-cheatsheet.md 35 lines · SHA-256 88da1683ef68
   1 # Frugal Fable — mid-task cheatsheet
   2 
   3 ## Route each slice (highest axis sets the floor; go up, never down)
   4 
   5 - Stakes ↑ (ships / architectural / security) · Reversibility ↑ (one-way / hard to test) · Ambiguity ↑ (needs judgment → Fable)
   6 
   7 | Slice | Model |
   8 |---|---|
   9 | scan / grep / inventory / log + test-output reduction / doc summary | Haiku |
  10 | bounded patch (well-specified) / adversarial verify / targeted tests | Sonnet (build+tests must pass) |
  11 | hard refactor / correctness- or security-critical / Sonnet struggled | Opus (Fable reviews diff) |
  12 | decompose / architect / coordinate shared files / integrate / final review | Fable (never delegate) |
  13 
  14 Conservative floor: architectural/high-stakes/one-way → Opus or Fable only. Unsure → go up one tier.
  15 
  16 ## Context firewall
  17 
  18 Delegated agent writes to `.frugal-fable/<task>/` and returns ONLY: `path + 3-line summary + confidence`.
  19 Fable reads files on demand at synthesis/review — never pulls all output into context up front.
  20 
  21 ## Harness
  22 
  23 1 slice / coupled / interactive → Fable direct. Few independent → inline `Agent`. Many independent → `Workflow` (out-of-context). Research → `deep-research-cheap` as-is.
  24 
  25 ## Handoff packet (every delegation)
  26 
  27 objective + repo path · in-scope / out-of-scope · where to write + what to return (path+summary+confidence, not full content) · verification commands + success criteria · stop conditions (mismatch / failed retry / needs out-of-scope → stop & report).
  28 
  29 ## Quality gate
  30 
  31 No delegated patch accepted until it passes the verification its stakes demand. Fable integrates + reviews the diff. Reports are leads, not facts — reopen cited files before relying on high-impact findings.
  32 
  33 ## Research tooling
  34 
  35 `bdata search` / `bdata scrape` / bdata data-feeds over built-in web tools (broader reach, fewer blocks, writes to file). Fall back to WebSearch/WebFetch.
SKILL.md 167 lines · SHA-256 a5b27756ef13
   1 ---
   2 name: frugal-fable
   3 description: Use when running on Claude Fable (or any premium model) and the work is token-heavy — building features, multi-file changes, research, testing, debugging, migrations, or anything spanning many files/sources. Keeps Fable on the judgment (decompose, architect, synthesize, review) and delegates bounded, verifiable heavy-lifting to cheaper models (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus) — with a quality floor so construction work is never owned by a weak agent. Triggers on requests to "be efficient with Fable", "don't burn tokens", orchestrate subagents, or delegate work. Also fires on cross-CLI delegation: "delegate to Codex", "use Codex/GPT for this", "second opinion from Codex", or offloading work to a separate Codex/ChatGPT quota.
   4 ---
   5 
   6 # Frugal Fable
   7 
   8 Fable is expensive because Fable is good. Spend it on judgment, not on scans,
   9 boilerplate, and log-reading. Delegate the heavy, repeatable, *verifiable* work
  10 to cheaper models — but never let a weak agent own quality-critical construction.
  11 
  12 **The deal:** cheaper agents *gather signal and produce candidate work to files*.
  13 Fable *decides, integrates, and reviews*. Truth-judgment and final quality stay
  14 with Fable, always.
  15 
  16 ## ⚠️ Turn Ultracode OFF before using this skill
  17 
  18 frugal-fable and **Ultracode are opposites** and must not run together.
  19 Ultracode's standing order is *"run a workflow for every task, token cost is not
  20 a constraint, be exhaustive, run several workflows in sequence, loop until
  21 nothing is left."* frugal-fable's whole purpose is to **conserve**. Run both and
  22 you get the worst case: cheap workers fan out, *and then* Fable launches extra
  23 exhaustive passes on top — which is exactly how usage gets blown (it has happened).
  24 
  25 - If Ultracode is on, **say so and stop** — ask the user to toggle it off (`/ultracode` or the toggle by the model selector), then proceed.
  26 - This skill is a *guide*, not a hard cap. A guide cannot beat Ultracode's "spend everything" directive. The only thing that truly enforces a ceiling is a **token budget in the workflow** (see Budget discipline). Use it.
  27 - After a delegated workflow returns, **do NOT autonomously launch a second "gap-fill" research round.** Read the saved files, synthesize, and stop. Widen scope only if the user asks.
  28 
  29 ## Budget discipline (the real brake)
  30 
  31 A skill convention biases behavior; it cannot force a spend limit. When the user
  32 is on a constrained usage window — or you're running unsupervised — use a
  33 workflow with a **hard token cap**, not just routing advice:
  34 
  35 - For research, use the bundled **`references/frugal-research.js`** workflow (hard caps: 4 angles / 8 fetches / 10 claims / 2 votes, a `budget.remaining()` gate that stops fanning out, synthesis pinned to Sonnet). Run it via the `Workflow` tool with `{scriptPath: "<abs path to references/frugal-research.js>"}`, or copy it to `~/.claude/workflows/frugal-research.js` to invoke by name. (If you also have the community `deep-research-cheap` workflow installed, that's the deeper, uncapped alternative for when you have headroom.)
  36 - In any custom `Workflow`, gate fan-out on `budget.remaining()` and keep a reserve for synthesis. See `references/fanout-template.js`.
  37 - **Scope is a cost lever.** A 6-lane, 12-question mega-prompt makes even "cheap" workflows expensive (verify fans out per claim). Split huge asks into focused runs, or cap the angles. Tell the user the tradeoff instead of silently fanning out to 100 agents.
  38 - "Cheap model" ≠ "cheap run." 75 Sonnet agents at ~27k each is still ~2M tokens. Watch the *count*, not just the per-agent tier.
  39 
  40 ## What stays with Fable (never delegated)
  41 
  42 - Decomposing ambiguous work into clean, independent slices.
  43 - Architecture, product, and safety tradeoffs.
  44 - Shared-file coordination and integrating partial work into one coherent whole.
  45 - Resolving conflicting subagent reports — deciding what's actually true.
  46 - Final review, risk assessment, and user-facing synthesis.
  47 
  48 ## Model routing — decide per slice, at runtime
  49 
  50 We don't know in advance what we're building, so route each slice when you reach
  51 it. Score it on three axes; the highest one sets the **floor** (you may always go
  52 higher, never lower):
  53 
  54 - **Stakes** — ships to prod? architectural? security/correctness-critical? → raises floor
  55 - **Reversibility** — one-way door, hard to test, destructive? → raises floor
  56 - **Ambiguity** — spec fuzzy, needs real judgment? → raises floor, often stays with Fable
  57 
  58 | Slice | Owner | Gate before Fable accepts |
  59 |---|---|---|
  60 | Scans, grep, repo/web inventory, log & test-output reduction, doc summaries | **Haiku** | low-stakes; sanity-check only |
  61 | Bounded, well-specified patches; adversarial verification; targeted tests | **Sonnet** | build + relevant tests pass |
  62 | Hard refactors, correctness/security-critical code, slices where Sonnet visibly struggles | **Opus** | Fable reviews the diff |
  63 | Any tier above, when the user has consented to Codex offload | **Codex** (tier-mapped — see `references/codex-delegation.md`) | same gate as the Claude tier it replaces |
  64 | Decompose, architect, coordinate, integrate, final review | **Fable** | — |
  65 
  66 **Conservative build floor (this project's default):** cheap models do mechanical
  67 work and bounded patches that come with passing tests. Anything architectural,
  68 high-stakes, or one-way stays with **Opus or Fable**. When unsure which tier, go
  69 up one — a re-run on a cheap model that wasn't good enough costs more than starting
  70 at the right tier.
  71 
  72 ## The second pool (Codex) — cross-CLI offload
  73 
  74 If the machine also has OpenAI's Codex CLI, its models run on a **separate
  75 subscription quota** — slices routed there consume no Claude usage at all.
  76 
  77 - **Consent gate — never assume.** The first time Codex routing would help,
  78   check `codex --version`. Present → ask the user: "Codex is available — want
  79   me to offload [named slices] to it? It won't touch your Claude usage."
  80   Not installed → don't mention Codex at all. Declined → stay on Claude
  81   models for the rest of the session without re-asking. Running unsupervised
  82   (user away, can't answer)? Don't block — proceed on Claude models and
  83   surface the Codex offer in your final summary for next time.
  84 - **Generous-quota routing.** Codex subscription limits are looser, so the
  85   second pool inverts the penny-pinching: default to its construction tier
  86   and escalate to its frontier tier freely for hard slices — never let a
  87   weak model own work to save quota that's ample.
  88 - Tier map, exact `codex exec` recipes, sandbox rules, and gotchas:
  89   `references/codex-delegation.md` — read it before the first Codex call.
  90 
  91 ## The context firewall (this is the main token saver)
  92 
  93 The thing that nukes Fable's budget is subagent output landing *in Fable's
  94 context*. So don't return it there.
  95 
  96 - Delegated agents **write findings/patches/logs to a scratch dir**
  97   (`.frugal-fable/<task>/` in the repo, gitignored) and **return only**:
  98   `path` + a 3-line summary + a confidence level.
  99 - Fable reads a file **on demand** — only the ones that matter, only at the moment
 100   it needs them (usually synthesis/review). Not all of them, not up front.
 101 - For research specifically, prefer tools that already write to file over ones that
 102   dump into context (the Bright Data skills do this — see Research lane).
 103 
 104 This keeps Fable's working set small even across dozens of subagents.
 105 
 106 ## Handoff packets
 107 
 108 Write every delegated prompt as if the agent has zero chat context. Include only:
 109 
 110 - Exact objective + the repo path.
 111 - In-scope files/surfaces, and what's explicitly **out of scope**.
 112 - **Where to write output** (the scratch path) and **what to return** (path + summary + confidence — *not* the full content).
 113 - Verification commands / browser flows to run, and what success looks like.
 114 - **Stop conditions:** if code doesn't match the prompt, a command fails after one
 115   retry, or the task needs out-of-scope files — stop and report, don't improvise.
 116 
 117 ## Choosing the harness — not every task needs a workflow
 118 
 119 - **1 slice, or tightly coupled / interactive** → Fable does it directly. No delegation; coordination cost would exceed savings.
 120 - **A few independent slices** → inline `Agent` calls (set the model per the table).
 121 - **Many independent slices / heavy fan-out** → author a `Workflow` (agents run *outside* Fable's context — cheapest). Adapt `references/fanout-template.js`.
 122 - **Research** → use `frugal-research` (hard budget cap) when usage is constrained or you're unsupervised; `deep-research-cheap` when you have headroom and want maximum depth. Don't rebuild either.
 123 
 124 ## Lanes (soft defaults, not rigid rules)
 125 
 126 - **Build/execute:** Fable plans + owns shared files, integration, and final review.
 127   Cheaper agents produce *candidate* bounded patches to the scratch dir with passing
 128   tests. **Quality gate:** no patch is accepted until it passes the verification its
 129   stakes demand (build, targeted tests, or Fable diff-review for high-stakes). Fable
 130   integrates and reviews — it never rubber-stamps a delegated diff.
 131 - **Research:** delegate to `deep-research-cheap` (Haiku collects via `bdata` + WebSearch,
 132   Sonnet verifies adversarially, Fable synthesizes). For one-off lookups, a single Haiku
 133   agent with `bdata search`/`bdata scrape` writing to a scratch file. Prefer `bdata` over
 134   built-in web tools — broader reach, fewer blocks, and the bdata skills output to file.
 135 - **Testing:** Fable names the validation direction and which checks matter. Lighter agents
 136   run targeted tests, browser flows, screenshots, and log reduction; report exact commands,
 137   failures, likely cause, and whether failures look real / flaky / environmental.
 138 - **Debugging:** cheaper agents cluster logs, reproduce, and try small fixes to files; Fable
 139   decides which diagnosis is trustworthy and owns the real fix.
 140 
 141 If a task is tiny, or the validation itself needs delicate judgment, keep it with Fable.
 142 
 143 ## Vetting delegated work
 144 
 145 Treat subagent reports as **leads, not facts**. Before relying on a high-impact
 146 finding, opening a PR, or telling the user it's done: reopen the cited file(s),
 147 confirm the line refs / failures, and review the final diff against the task.
 148 Let lighter agents gather signal; keep truth-judgment with Fable.
 149 
 150 ## References
 151 
 152 - `references/frugal-research.js` — budget-capped research `Workflow` (Haiku collect → Sonnet
 153   verify → Sonnet synthesize, hard caps + token gate). Run via the `Workflow` tool with
 154   `{scriptPath}`, or copy to `~/.claude/workflows/` to invoke by name. Requires a Fable-class
 155   runtime that exposes the `Workflow` tool.
 156 - `references/fanout-template.js` — adaptable `Workflow` script for the general fan-out case
 157   (route by model, verify, synthesize). Copy and adapt per task; don't run blind.
 158 - `references/routing-cheatsheet.md` — one-screen version of the routing table + firewall
 159   protocol for quick recall mid-task.
 160 
 161 ## Credits
 162 
 163 Adapted from BuilderIO's `efficient-fable` skill, extended here with explicit model tiers, a
 164 conservative build-quality floor, the file-based context firewall, harness selection, and a
 165 budget-capped research workflow (`frugal-research.js`). Lanes: research, build/dev, testing,
 166 debugging. As with all delegation, the orchestrator verifies delegated work before relying on
 167 it — see **Vetting delegated work** above. That review step is the point, not an afterthought.
Review method, validation and use of the revisions

What the evidence supports

The original Windows regression run completed 56 tests: 50 passed and 6 failed. The revised repository suite completed 56: 53 passed and 3 legacy POSIX shell fixtures skipped. The separate portable regression suite passed 15 tests and the delegation scheduler passed 10 mocked-adapter tests. See machine-readable validation, original run, revised repository run, new Python tests, and scheduler tests.

All five revised skill folders were checked with the skill-creator frontmatter validator. Python helpers were syntax-checked; source-file links and tabs were checked in a browser. The final browser record is browser-validation.json. The independent forward review assesses realistic scenarios; its discovered issues were corrected and independently rechecked. These are static/inert exercises rather than a live agent-quality benchmark.

Browser validation covers tab/keyboard interactions, expandable evidence, link targets and desktop/mobile geometry. The original review did not obtain a pixel screenshot. Publication subsequently added a headless-Chrome rendered preview; hosted checks are recorded in live-browser-validation.json.

How to use this package

  1. Choose the skill tab, read its gaps and remaining limits, and inspect its complete revision/diff.
  2. Download that skill’s ZIP or the combined revised package. Each skill folder is self-contained. These are local review editions, not upstream releases.
  3. In your harness, choose one edition of a skill to avoid duplicate names and ambiguous routing. Follow that harness’s installation interface. No global skill/configuration files were changed here.
  4. For Windows, prefer the quoted Python commands in the revised references. Do not assume a bare bash command selects Git Bash. The macOS artifact helper remains optional and limited.
  5. Before real use, keep the stated authorization boundary and verify any runtime/provider capability the skill depends on. A validated folder is not a certified workflow.

Corrections versus mitigation

Scanner truncation, path separators, unsafe “safe” examples, conflicting PRD references and the workflow’s acceptance/accounting mechanics have concrete replacement code or documents. Source/deployment equivalence, OS-level sandboxing, registry pagination, hostile filesystem races, true provider budget enforcement and model-quality calibration remain explicit limits. The report does not claim those hard problems were solved by wording changes.

Primary references checked for this review

  • Node.js vm documentation: the module is not a security mechanism for untrusted code.
  • MCP 2025-11-25 security guidance and transports: used as a named protocol baseline; target versions need their own checks.
  • Python ZIP documentation: untrusted archive handling requires inspection and bounded extraction.
  • Amazon SES: verifies the service-category correction in the PRD reference.

Verification date: 12 October 2026. Source files and past changelog claims are distinguished from current local test outcomes. No creator-reputation or comprehensive vulnerability-corpus assessment was performed.

Original snapshot + revised folders + unified diffs + source hashes + offline regression evidence. No external assets or analytics are loaded by this HTML file.
